items.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 16 at 10:44AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
Strong northwesterly winds have developed across Shelikof Strait
and the waters around western Kodiak Island. These winds are
resuspending ash from the 1912 Katmai-Novarupta eruption, causing
haze and potentially trace amounts of ash accumulation. Villages
along western Kodiak Island are most likely to be impacted.

Those in sensitive groups or with respiratory ailments are
encouraged to avoid or reduce outdoor activity to avoid inhaling
the ash. The winds should weaken Saturday night.
items.areas: Kodiak Island Northeast; Kodiak Island Southwest

items.headline: High Wind Watch issued November 16 at 6:42AM AKST until November 17 at 6:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
items.description:
* WHAT...West winds 45 to 55 mph with gusts up to 75 mph possible.

* WHERE...Shemya and Attu Islands.

* WHEN...From this evening through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...High winds could move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel could be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds rapidly increase in strength late Monday
evening and peak early Tuesday morning as a strong low pressure
system moves through the Bering. Winds will lighten through Tuesday
afternoon.
items.instruction:
A high wind watch means there is potential for a hazardous high wind
event. Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates on this
situation. Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location
prior to the onset of winds.

* WHEN...From late Tuesday night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Moderate coastal flooding is possible. Roads may be
closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.
